entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: Ps 83:1-18 . Of Asaph --(See on Ps 74:1 , title). The historical occasion is probably that of 2Ch 20:1, 2 (compare Ps 47:1-9; 48:1-14 ). After a general petition, the craft and rage of the combined enemies are described, God's former dealings recited, and a like summary and speedy destruction on them is invoked.

entries.heading: 2. thine enemies
entries.text: 2. thine enemies --as well as ours ( Ps 74:23; Isa 37:23 ).

entries.heading: 3. hidden ones
entries.text: 3. hidden ones --whom God specially protects ( Ps 27:5; 91:1 ).

entries.heading: 4. from being a nation
entries.text: 4. from being a nation --utter destruction ( Isa 7:8; 23:1 ). Israel --here used for Judah, having been the common name.

entries.heading: 5. they have consulted
entries.text: 5. they have consulted --with heart, or cordially. together --all alike.

entries.heading: 6-8. tabernacles
entries.text: 6-8. tabernacles --for people ( Ps 78:67 ). they --all these united with the children of Lot, or Ammonites and Moabites (compare 2Ch 20:1 ).

9-11. Compare the similar fate of these ( 2Ch 20:23 ) with that of the foes mentioned in Jud 7:22 , here referred to. They destroyed one another ( Jud 4:6-24; 7:25 ). Human remains form manure (compare 2Ki 9:37; Jer 9:22 ).
12. The language of the invaders. houses --literally, "residences," enclosures, as for flocks ( Ps 65:12 ). of God --as the proprietors of the land ( 2Ch 20:11; Isa 14:25 ).

entries.heading: 13. like a wheel
entries.text: 13. like a wheel --or, whirling of any light thing ( Isa 17:13 ), as stubble or chaff ( Ps 1:4 ).
14, 15. Pursue them to an utter destruction.

entries.heading: 16. that they may seek
entries.text: 16. that they may seek --or as Ps 83:18 , supply "men," since Ps 83:17, 18 amplify the sentiment of Ps 83:16 , expressing more fully the measure of destruction, and the lesson of God's being and perfections (compare 2Ch 20:29 ) taught to all men.
